title: Pre-label review QA: survival of model boxes after human review
scenario: Compare reviewer-corrected boxes (xyxy) with model pre-labels (COCO xywh) by box id: accepted at IoU >= 0.9 on continuous coordinates, otherwise adjusted, relabeled or deleted. Test 2 lists added and out-of-bounds boxes.

verified.why_correct: Strict comparisons are right for continuous coordinates: a box with x_max == width (img-05/B9 ends at 800) sits exactly on the edge and is inside, as the README says. `>=` would wrongly flag it.

bugs.title: Zero coordinate treated as blank
bugs.old: if any(c is None for c in coords):
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_street_outcomes: img-03/B5 is 'deleted' instead of 'accepted'. Everything else matches.
bugs.why: all() treats 0.0 as false, so a review box touching the left edge (x_min = 0) is dropped as if a coordinate were blank. Its pre-label then has no reviewed box and shows as deleted.
hints: img-03/B5 shows deleted, but reviews.csv has a row for it. What is special about that row?
Look at how load_reviews decides a row has a blank coordinate.
`not all(coords)` is true for 0.0; use any(c is None for c in coords).
probes: Why does parse_coord return None for blanks instead of 0.0, and why does that matter here?
Which other values would `all()` treat as missing?

bugs.title: Pixel-inclusive +1 on continuous coordinates
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_warehouse_outcomes: img-05/B8 is 'accepted' instead of 'adjusted'. Every other outcome is unchanged.
bugs.why: The README defines continuous coordinates, so width is x_max − x_min. Adding 1 to every span inflates both the areas and the intersection, which pushes IoU toward 1. For the narrow B8 pallet that moves IoU from 0.897 to 0.902, over the 0.9 line.
hints: img-05/B8 is accepted. Work out its IoU by hand from the data.
Check how widths and heights are computed in geometry.py against the README's geometry section.
span() returns hi - lo + 1; it should be hi - lo.
probes: Why did only one box change category when every IoU moved?
Does the +1 make IoU larger or smaller for overlapping boxes, and why?

bugs.title: Clipping mutates the reviewer's original boxes
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_out_of_bounds: [] instead of [['img-01', None, 'sign'], ['img-09', 'B15', 'car']]. Outcomes and added counts are unaffected.
bugs.why: copy.copy of a list makes a new list holding the same Box objects, so clipping changes the original reviewed boxes in place. By the time the out-of-bounds check reads the originals they've already been clipped, so nothing is out of bounds.
hints: out_of_bounds is empty, but img-09/B15 clearly goes past x = 640 in reviews.csv. What does the box look like when the check runs?
evaluate() keeps `revs` for the check and `clipped` for IoU. Are they really different boxes?
clip_to_image uses copy.copy(boxes); it needs copy.deepcopy(boxes).
probes: Why didn't any outcome change even though the boxes were mutated?
What other fix (in clip_to_image's loop) would work without deepcopy?

context_qa.q: How are pre-labels converted to corner coordinates?
context_qa.a: `from_xywh` reads `[x, y, w, h]` as floats and builds `Box(x1=x, y1=y, x2=x + w, y2=y + h)`.

context_qa.q: What does evaluate() do per image?
context_qa.a: For each image id in sorted order it clips that image's pre-labels and reviewed boxes with `clip_to_image`, maps reviewed boxes by box id (only ids that exist among the pre-labels), classifies every pre-label, counts the rest as added, and then runs `is_out_of_bounds` over the image's reviewed boxes from `rev_by_image`.

It parses the four coordinates with `parse_coord` (blank → None, otherwise float) and skips a row when its coordinate check fails. All kept rows become Box objects with normalised image, box id and label.
`iou` takes the overlap span on each axis (floored at 0), multiplies them for the intersection, and divides by area(a) + area(b) − intersection. Both overlap and area use `span(lo, hi)`.

context_qa.q: What is in the report's outcomes dict?
context_qa.a: It groups the per-pre-label outcomes by the image's dataset (`street`, `warehouse`), with keys like `img-05/B8` and values `accepted`, `adjusted`, `relabeled` or `deleted`.
A list of boxes with x values clamped into [0, width] and y values into [0, height]. It copies the input list first and then sets the coordinates on the boxes in that copy.
